stem:
You are the obstetrics registrar. A 34 year old primipara has had a spontaneous vaginal birth 15 minutes ago at 40 weeks after augmentation for prolonged first stage. Estimated blood loss so far is 900 mL and continues to trickle.

Her booking blood pressure was 128/82. She developed gestational hypertension at 36 weeks and has been on labetalol 200 mg twice daily. Blood pressure in early labour was 152/98 and again 156/102 in second stage. She has no known allergies.

On examination the uterus feels boggy. The placenta appears complete on inspection. The perineum is intact. Intramuscular oxytocin 10 units was given with the anterior shoulder and a 40 unit oxytocin infusion in 1 L Hartmann is now running at 250 mL/hour. Uterine massage continues.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 108, BP 156/98, RR 20, SpO2 99% room air, temperature 37.1
data_table.Uterine tone: Boggy on abdominal palpation despite massage
data_table.Uterotonics given: IM oxytocin 10 units at anterior shoulder; oxytocin 40 units in 1 L Hartmann infusion at 250 mL/hour
data_table.Blood pressure trend: Gestational hypertension on labetalol 200 mg BD; BP 152/98 then 156/102 in second stage

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next uterotonic to add?

options.text: Carboprost (15 methyl PGF2 alpha) 250 microgram intramuscular, up to 8 doses at 15 minute intervals
options.rationale: In PPH with atony and a hypertensive contraindication to ergometrine, carboprost 250 microgram IM is the appropriate second line uterotonic and can be repeated to a maximum of 8 doses; asthma is the main contraindication (Source: RANZCOG Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage).

options.text: Ergometrine 250 microgram intramuscular immediately as a second line uterotonic
options.rationale: Ergometrine is contraindicated in hypertensive disease because it can precipitate a severe surge in blood pressure and cerebrovascular events (Source: RANZCOG Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage).

options.text: Misoprostol 800 microgram sublingual as the second line uterotonic after oxytocin infusion
options.rationale: Misoprostol is a third line uterotonic in Australian PPH pathways; its onset is slower and it is often used only when parenteral options are exhausted or unavailable (Source: RANZCOG Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage).

options.text: Tranexamic acid 1 g intravenous over 10 minutes and stop further uterotonics
options.rationale: Tranexamic acid is an important adjunct within 3 hours of onset per WOMAN and Australian guidance but does not replace ongoing uterotonic escalation while atony persists (Source: RANZCOG Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage).

options.text: Insert a Bakri intrauterine balloon before any further pharmacological escalation
options.rationale: Balloon tamponade is a mechanical adjunct after pharmacological measures have failed to control atony; escalation of uterotonics with an appropriate agent takes priority now (Source: RANZCOG Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage).

explanation.summary: Atonic PPH continues despite oxytocin. Ergometrine is contraindicated in hypertensive disease so the appropriate second line uterotonic is carboprost 250 microgram IM, repeated up to 8 doses. Tranexamic acid is a parallel adjunct. Balloon tamponade is a step later in the pathway.
key_points: Carboprost 250 microgram IM up to 8 doses is the appropriate second line uterotonic when ergometrine is contraindicated.
TXA 1 g IV within 3 hours is an adjunct, not a substitute for uterotonics.
explanation.pearls: For PPH atony in a hypertensive woman, carboprost 250 microgram IM (up to 8 doses) is the second line uterotonic because ergometrine is contraindicated.

subtopic_detail: Methotrexate versus surgery for tubal ectopic
stem:
You are the gynaecology registrar in the early pregnancy assessment unit. A 28 year old woman presents at 6+3 weeks by her last menstrual period with left iliac fossa discomfort and light vaginal spotting for 2 days.

This is her first pregnancy. She has no significant medical history, no allergies, and takes only pregnancy multivitamins. She lives with her partner in the city, has reliable transport, and works from home for the next 4 weeks.

On examination her abdomen is soft with mild left iliac fossa tenderness only. There is no rebound. Speculum shows a closed cervix with a small amount of dark blood. Bimanual is uncomfortable in the left adnexa without a definite mass.

Vital signs: pulse 82, blood pressure 118/74, respiratory rate 16, SpO2 99% in room air, temperature 36.7. Beta hCG is 2100 IU/L; a repeat 48 hours ago was 2280 IU/L. Transvaginal ultrasound shows an empty uterus with an endometrial thickness of 8 mm and a 22 mm left tubal mass without foetal cardiac activity. Full blood count, renal, and liver function tests are within normal limits.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 82, BP 118/74, RR 16, SpO2 99% room air, temperature 36.7
data_table.Ultrasound: Empty uterus; endometrial thickness 8 mm; 22 mm left tubal mass; no foetal cardiac activity; no significant free fluid
data_table.Blood tests: FBC, UEC, LFTs within normal limits
data_table.Social: Reliable transport; works from home for next 4 weeks; lives with partner

lead_in: What is the most appropriate initial management?

options.text: Laparoscopic salpingectomy today because any tubal ectopic requires surgical management once diagnosed
options.rationale: RANZCOG reserves surgery for bhCG 5000 IU/L or above, foetal cardiac activity, a mass 3.5 cm or larger, significant pain, haemodynamic instability, or unreliable follow up; this case does not meet these thresholds (Source: RANZCOG GPS Ectopic Pregnancy).

options.text: Intramuscular methotrexate 50 mg/m2 with weekly beta hCG surveillance to day 7 and beyond until it is negative
options.rationale: This tubal ectopic meets RANZCOG criteria for medical management: bhCG under 5000 IU/L, no foetal cardiac activity, mass under 3.5 cm, minimal pain, no haemorrhage, reliable follow up, and no contraindications; single dose methotrexate is appropriate (Source: RANZCOG GPS Ectopic Pregnancy).

options.text: Serial beta hCG monitoring alone every 48 hours with expectant management for the next 2 weeks
options.rationale: Expectant management is reserved for suspected declining or resolving pregnancy of unknown location; a visualised 22 mm tubal mass warrants active treatment rather than watchful waiting (Source: RANZCOG GPS Ectopic Pregnancy).

options.text: Mifepristone 200 mg orally followed by misoprostol 800 microgram vaginally to complete a medical management pathway
options.rationale: Mifepristone plus misoprostol is a first trimester medical abortion regimen for intrauterine pregnancy and has no role in tubal ectopic management (Source: RANZCOG GPS Ectopic Pregnancy).

options.text: Laparoscopic salpingostomy to preserve tubal patency for future fertility as a first line treatment
options.rationale: Salpingostomy is a fertility sparing surgical option but is not preferred over methotrexate in this stable candidate meeting all medical criteria (Source: RANZCOG GPS Ectopic Pregnancy).

explanation.summary: Tubal ectopic meeting the RANZCOG medical criteria (bhCG below 5000 IU/L, no cardiac activity, mass below 3.5 cm, minimal pain, reliable follow up, no contraindications) is treated with single dose methotrexate 50 mg/m2 IM. Weekly bhCG to day 7 and to negativity monitors response. Surgery is reserved for cases above these thresholds or unstable.
key_points: RANZCOG surgical threshold for tubal ectopic is bhCG 5000 IU/L or above.
Methotrexate is preferred when all medical criteria are met.
Expectant management is only for suspected resolving pregnancy of unknown location.
explanation.pearls: For tubal ectopic with bhCG under 5000 IU/L, mass under 3.5 cm, no cardiac activity, minimal pain and reliable follow up, single dose methotrexate 50 mg/m2 IM is the RANZCOG choice.

stem:
You are the general practice registrar reviewing a Cervical Screening Test result for a 32 year old woman. She had a self collected vaginal swab through the general practice 5 days ago and this is her first screening test.

She is well, has a regular sexual partner of 3 years, and uses combined oral contraceptive pills. Her last cervical screening prior to today was never; she was overseas during the transition from Pap smear to the NCSP renewed program. She has no dyspareunia and no post coital bleeding.

The report reads: HPV detected, other high risk type (not 16 or 18). Because the sample is self collected there is no liquid based cytology reported on this sample.

data_table.History: 32 y, first ever cervical screen; no post coital or intermenstrual bleeding
data_table.Sample: Self collected vaginal swab; no cytology reported on self collected sample
data_table.Result: HPV detected, non 16/18 high risk type

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step under the National Cervical Screening Program?

options.text: Repeat the self collected HPV test in 12 months without cytology and manage on the future HPV result
options.rationale: Repeat testing at 12 months without intervening cytology risks missing a prevalent high grade lesion; the NCSP requires cytology triage now (Source: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines).
source_refs: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines

options.text: Refer directly to colposcopy today because any HPV positive self collected sample requires colposcopy
options.rationale: Direct colposcopy from a self collected sample is only recommended for HPV 16 or 18 detected; non 16/18 types go via clinician collected cytology first (Source: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines).
source_refs: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines

options.text: Recall for a clinician collected cervical sample for reflex liquid based cytology and act on that cytology result
options.rationale: Under the NCSP, a self collected sample positive for HPV non 16/18 requires clinician collected liquid based cytology; if cytology is negative or low grade she returns for repeat HPV testing in 12 months, and high grade cytology triggers colposcopy (Source: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines).
source_refs: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines

options.text: Recall for a clinician collected sample to repeat HPV testing rather than proceed to cytology triage this cycle
options.rationale: Repeating HPV testing on a clinician sample does not add triage value; the NCSP pathway uses liquid based cytology at this step (Source: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines).
source_refs: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines

options.text: Reassure the woman that non 16 or 18 HPV clears spontaneously and rescreen at the routine 5 year interval
options.rationale: Rescreening at 5 years is only appropriate when HPV is not detected; any HPV detected result requires prompt triage rather than deferral (Source: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines).
source_refs: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines

explanation.summary: For a self collected NCSP sample with non 16/18 high risk HPV, the next step is clinician collected liquid based cytology to triage. Colposcopy is reserved for HPV 16 or 18 detected on self collection, or for high grade cytology. Rescreening at 5 years applies only when HPV is not detected.
key_points: Self collected HPV 16/18 detected: direct colposcopy.
Self collected non 16/18 HPV detected: clinician cytology triage.
Rescreen at 5 years only if HPV not detected.
explanation.pearls: Self collected non 16/18 HPV detected on the NCSP goes to clinician collected liquid based cytology triage, not straight to colposcopy.

sources.label: NCSP National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines
RACGP Red Book preventive activities in general practice

stem:
You are the obstetric registrar reviewing a 27 year old primigravida at 34+2 weeks who presented with headache and one episode of blurred vision.

Her booking blood pressure was 118/70 and 20 week anomaly ultrasound was reported as normal. Since 32 weeks she has been reviewed weekly for a rising blood pressure trend and was commenced on labetalol 200 mg twice daily 3 days ago.

On arrival tonight she is clinically well but reports a persistent frontal headache and one flash of blurred vision that has settled. There are no visible papilloedema, no epigastric tenderness, and no clonus. Deep tendon reflexes are 3+ in the lower limbs. Foetal cardiotocograph shows a baseline of 145, moderate variability, and accelerations without decelerations.

Vital signs: pulse 92, blood pressure 178/112 (repeat 172/108 after 15 minutes), respiratory rate 18, SpO2 99% in room air, temperature 36.8. Urine dipstick shows 3+ protein. Full blood count, platelets 145, liver function tests within normal limits, urea 4.2, creatinine 68.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 92, BP 178/112 then 172/108, RR 18, SpO2 99% room air, temperature 36.8
data_table.Foetal CTG: Baseline 145, moderate variability, accelerations, no decelerations
data_table.Examination: Frontal headache; one settled visual disturbance; brisk reflexes; no clonus, no papilloedema, no epigastric tenderness
data_table.Investigations: Urine dipstick 3+ protein; platelets 145 x10^9/L; LFTs within normal limits; UEC within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next intervention?

options.text: Commence sublingual nifedipine 10 mg immediately as the initial antihypertensive with reassessment every 5 minutes
options.rationale: Sublingual nifedipine is not recommended in pregnancy because of unpredictable rapid falls in blood pressure; oral immediate release nifedipine or IV labetalol or hydralazine is preferred (Source: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy).
source_refs: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy

options.text: Increase oral labetalol from 200 mg twice daily to 400 mg three times daily and reassess her blood pressure in 60 minutes
options.rationale: Oral titration is inadequate for a persistent systolic 170 mmHg or above with neurological symptoms; intravenous antihypertensive plus MgSO4 is required (Source: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy).
source_refs: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy

options.text: Administer betamethasone 11.4 mg intramuscular for foetal lung maturation and defer any other intervention for 24 hours
options.rationale: Betamethasone is appropriate for a 34+2 weeks pregnancy but does not replace urgent MgSO4 and antihypertensive; delay risks eclampsia and stroke (Source: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy).
source_refs: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy

options.text: Intravenous magnesium sulfate 4 g load over 20 minutes then 1 g/hour infusion, alongside intravenous antihypertensive
options.rationale: This is severe pre-eclampsia with neurological symptoms; the SOMANZ Australian pathway loads magnesium sulfate 4 g IV over 20 minutes then 1 g/hour to prevent eclampsia while urgent BP control is initiated (Source: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy).
source_refs: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy

options.text: Proceed straight to caesarean section within 30 minutes without magnesium sulfate loading or antihypertensive control first
options.rationale: Stabilisation with MgSO4 and BP control precedes delivery except in acute maternal compromise or unreassuring CTG; the CTG is reassuring so stabilisation is first (Source: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy).
source_refs: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy

explanation.summary: Severe pre-eclampsia with neurological symptoms at 34+2 weeks requires MgSO4 for eclampsia prevention (4 g IV load over 20 minutes then 1 g/hour) alongside urgent intravenous BP control. Betamethasone is worth giving but does not replace stabilisation. Sublingual nifedipine is avoided. Delivery is planned after stabilisation.
key_points: SOMANZ MgSO4 load 4 g IV over 20 minutes then 1 g/hour.
Intravenous labetalol or hydralazine or oral IR nifedipine, not sublingual nifedipine.
Betamethasone given but does not defer treatment.
explanation.pearls: In severe pre-eclampsia with neurological symptoms, MgSO4 4 g IV over 20 minutes then 1 g/hour is the SOMANZ eclampsia prophylaxis regimen alongside IV antihypertensive.

sources.label: SOMANZ Guideline for the Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy

stem:
You are the antenatal registrar. A 29 year old woman at 34+4 weeks gestation in her second pregnancy presents with 10 days of generalised itch that is worse on her palms and soles at night.

Her first pregnancy 3 years ago was complicated by cholestasis diagnosed at 35 weeks and induced at 37 weeks; the baby was well. Her booking bloods, morphology, and glucose tolerance were within normal limits.

On examination she is well with no rash and no jaundice. Foetal movements are normal. Cardiotocograph shows a baseline of 138 with moderate variability, accelerations, and no decelerations.

Vital signs: pulse 84, blood pressure 118/72, respiratory rate 16, SpO2 99% in room air, temperature 36.7. Bloods this morning show ALT 118 U/L (5-40), ALP 320 U/L (30-120, elevated in pregnancy), GGT 92 U/L (5-40), bilirubin 12 micromol/L, fasting bile acids 62 micromol/L, INR 1.0, platelets 240.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 84, BP 118/72, RR 16, SpO2 99% room air, temperature 36.7
data_table.Foetal CTG: Baseline 138, moderate variability, accelerations, no decelerations
data_table.Liver panel: ALT 118 U/L (5-40); GGT 92 U/L (5-40); bilirubin 12 micromol/L; fasting bile acids 62 micromol/L; ALP 320 U/L (elevated in pregnancy expected)
data_table.Past obstetric: Cholestasis in prior pregnancy at 35 weeks, induced at 37 weeks with well infant

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management plan?

options.text: Reassure the woman that her pruritus is due to normal pregnancy skin changes and manage with emollients only
options.rationale: Fasting bile acids 62 micromol/L with elevated transaminases confirms cholestasis and requires structured surveillance and pharmacotherapy (Source: RCOG Green top 43 Obstetric cholestasis).

options.text: Commence ursodeoxycholic acid 500 mg twice daily and continue expectant management to spontaneous labour beyond 40 weeks
options.rationale: Stillbirth risk rises with gestation and bile acid concentration; expectant management beyond 40 weeks is inconsistent with Australian centre practice at this bile acid level (Source: RCOG Green top 43 Obstetric cholestasis).

options.text: Commence oral vitamin K 10 mg daily, chlorpheniramine 4 mg at night, and repeat liver and bile acid bloods in 2 weeks
options.rationale: Vitamin K is only indicated if the INR is prolonged; her INR is normal and delaying escalation to definitive management is inappropriate (Source: RCOG Green top 43 Obstetric cholestasis).

options.text: Deliver immediately by category one caesarean section because bile acids above 40 micromol/L mandate expedited birth today
options.rationale: Bile acids in the 40 to 99 range warrant birth by 35 to 36 weeks and not immediate delivery, so vaginal induction is preferred when there is no other indication for caesarean (Source: RCOG Green top 43 Obstetric cholestasis).

options.text: Ursodeoxycholic acid 500 mg twice daily, weekly bile acids, and plan delivery by 36 weeks given peak bile acids of 62
options.rationale: RCOG and Australian centres bring forward delivery to 35 to 36 weeks when peak fasting bile acids are 40 to 99 micromol/L because of a threefold rise in stillbirth risk from 37 weeks onward; UDCA relieves pruritus and biochemistry (Source: RCOG Green top 43 Obstetric cholestasis; Ovadia meta-analysis Lancet 2019).

explanation.summary: This is obstetric cholestasis with peak fasting bile acids in the 40 to 99 micromol/L band. Ursodeoxycholic acid is used for pruritus and biochemistry, and delivery is brought forward to 35 to 36 weeks because stillbirth risk rises steeply beyond that with these bile acid values. Vitamin K only substitutes when the INR is prolonged and expectant management to 40 weeks is not consistent with current Australian practice.
key_points: Peak fasting bile acids 40-99 micromol/L: aim delivery by 35-36 weeks.
Peak fasting bile acids over 100 micromol/L: consider birth by 34-35 weeks.
UDCA relieves symptoms; vitamin K only if INR prolonged.
explanation.pearls: In obstetric cholestasis, peak fasting bile acids 40 to 99 micromol/L bring the delivery target forward to 35 to 36 weeks; above 100 micromol/L consider 34 to 35 weeks.
